key_insight: MRI radiomic features improved survival prediction beyond clinical variables in lung cancer brain metastases and were associated with tumor immune features.
clinical_relevance: These biomarkers could refine prognostic risk stratification, but the study does not establish treatment-selection or drug-discovery benefits.
method: Retrospective analysis of 103 patients with matched preoperative MRI and histopathology.
Combined contrast-enhanced T1 and T2-FLAIR radiomics with clinical variables using Cox, random survival forest, and DeepSurv models.
Evaluated overall survival, CNS progression, and leptomeningeal progression; compared imaging-only risk groups with immune pathology.
evidence_signal: The clinical-imaging DeepSurv model achieved an overall-survival concordance index of 0.728; endpoint-specific risk groups separated overall survival (26.7 vs. 9.1 months) and leptomeningeal progression, but not CNS progression.
watch_item: The small retrospective cohort and lack of external validation reported in the abstract limit confidence in generalizability.
paper_title: MRI Biomarkers for Brain Metastases in Lung Cancer Using Machine Learning
